questions.question: Which scope should the BUG-337 fix take? Orientation found BK-456 (split) and BK-457 (RFC-0022 prune) constrain it: fix the contradictions now so the split stays a pure move, and leave the mechanism and history prose alone. No failing test is possible: test_atomic.py already asserts move/copy onto a file gives AlreadyExists on every backend.

options.label: 4 fixes + BE-028 (Recommended)
options.description: BE-021 row 2 drops `move`/`copy` dst, and row 1 gains it (dst is a directory gives InvalidPath; dst ancestor is a file is already row 6). BE-008 states the full order once: closed guard, root, WR-010 gate (where the class runs it: on the kernel per BE-030, off it at the Store), path validity, overwrite, I/O. BE-010 links to it. BE-018/BE-019 bind the dst-is-a-directory rule to BE-021's hierarchical scope. Rewording BE-028's 'serialised by the kernel' to 'by the operating system'. Spec-only, no CHANGELOG.

options.label: 4 fixes only
options.description: Same as above, but leave BE-028's 'kernel' wording for BK-456's prune. Smaller diff; the wording hazard stays.

options.label: Fold into BK-456
options.description: Close nothing now and fix during the split. Breaks BK-456's 'pure move, no clause reworded' gate, so not advised.
